title: The Cost of Money
headline_read: Borrowing is still expensive — rates remain elevated.

indicators.title: Federal Funds Rate
indicators.context: The interest rate the Federal Reserve sets to steer the economy — the anchor for nearly every other rate, from savings accounts to business loans.
indicators.read: The Fed's policy rate is 4.33%, and easing as the Fed pivots toward cuts.

indicators.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield
indicators.context: The yield on 10-year U.S. government debt — the benchmark that drives mortgage rates and long-term borrowing costs across the economy.
indicators.read: Now 4.38%, little changed over the past year.

indicators.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield
indicators.context: The yield on 2-year government debt — closely tied to where investors expect the Fed to set rates over the next couple of years.
indicators.read: Now 4.08%, little changed over the past year.

indicators.title: 30-Year Fixed Mortgage Rate
indicators.context: The average rate on a 30-year fixed home loan — the single biggest driver of housing affordability for most buyers.
indicators.read: 30-year mortgages are at 6.84%, keeping home affordability stretched.

indicators.title: Yield Curve · 10-Year minus 2-Year
indicators.context: The gap between 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields. When it turns negative, short-term borrowing costs more than long-term — a sign markets expect the Fed to cut rates ahead.
indicators.read: The curve recently un-inverted to +0.30 after an extended inversion. Recessions historically begin after the curve climbs back above zero — a reason for more vigilance, not less.
